title: Google Play Reviews

appIds.title: Package names
appIds.description: Android package names, e.g. ["com.whatsapp", "com.spotify.music"] — the id= part of any Google Play URL, and what an earlier run's app_id gives you. Use for "reviews of com.whatsapp". App names are not accepted (Play has no open search API): open the app's Play page and copy the id. A package that is not on Play in a country costs nothing: its status row says not_found. Each package is read for every language × country pair.
appIds.sectionDescription: Package names and/or Google Play URLs — at least one. Every app is read for every language in languages and every country in countries.

appUrls.title: Google Play URLs
appUrls.description: Google Play app pages, e.g. ["https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.whatsapp"]. Only the package name is read from the URL; its hl and gl are NOT used — languages and countries decide which locales are read. A URL from another site ends the run before anything is charged. A URL and its package name are the same app and are read once.

languages.title: Languages
languages.description: Play language codes (hl), e.g. ["en", "de", "pt-BR", "ja", "zh-TW"]; default ["en"]. Use ["zh-TW"] with countries=["tw"] for the tested Taiwan example. Each app is read for every language × country pair; rows carry the request language. Reviews retain source text (no actor translation). A review listed under two languages is delivered and billed once. Cost scales with apps × languages × countries × maxReviewsPerApp.

countries.title: Countries
countries.description: Play country codes (gl), e.g. ["us", "gb", "in", "br"]; default ["us"]. Any two-letter code; every row carries country. Google decides what it shows under each language × country pair, so the same review can appear under several (delivered and billed once; the status row counts duplicates). Name the markets the app has users in; one language and one country is the cheapest run.

maxReviewsPerApp.title: Max reviews per app, language and country
maxReviewsPerApp.description: Reviews to read per app, language AND country, e.g. 200; default 100; 0 = every review Google pages out (hundreds of thousands for big apps: cap the run with maxTotalChargeUsd). The main cost control: at most N × $0.004 per pair. The filters apply to these N reads, so 300 with maxRating 2 delivers the 1-2 star reviews among the 300 read — except when minRating = maxRating: that star value is filtered by Google itself and N reviews of that star are delivered. Google answers up to 100 per request.
maxReviewsPerApp.sectionDescription: How many reviews per app and locale, in what order, and which ones are worth paying for. The filters run before billing.

sort.title: Order
sort.description: "most_recent" (default; schedule this), "most_relevant" (Google Play's own order), "rating" (5-star first). Applied by Google before maxReviewsPerApp: "most_recent" with 100 reads the 100 newest reviews of each language × country pair. There is no lowest-rating-first order: for complaints use maxRating, or minRating = maxRating = 1.

minRating.title: Only reviews rated at least
minRating.description: 0 (default) = no lower bound. 1-5 = keep only reviews with at least this many stars, e.g. 4 for praise only. Set minRating and maxRating to the SAME value (both 1 for one-star reviews) and Google filters server-side: the other reviews are never fetched and the N read are all that star. Otherwise applied after the read and before billing; filtered reviews are never charged (the status row counts them in filtered).

maxRating.title: Only reviews rated at most
maxRating.description: 0 (default) = no upper bound. 1-5 = keep only reviews with at most this many stars, e.g. 2 for a complaints feed that pays nothing for the happy ones. Applied before billing; must be at least minRating. Use for "negative reviews", "complaints"; for exactly one star value set minRating = maxRating (filtered by Google, nothing is fetched to be discarded).

sinceDate.title: Only reviews on or after
sinceDate.description: Empty (default) = all dates. Keep only reviews on or after this day: "2026-09-01", or relative to the run day so a schedule never goes stale: "7 days", "2 weeks", "3 months", "yesterday". For a daily new-reviews feed pass "1 day" with sort "most_recent". Applied before billing; older reviews that were read are not charged. There is no end date and no "since last run" memory: dedupe on review_id downstream.

requireText.title: Only reviews with written text
requireText.description: false (default) = keep every review. true = drop reviews that are a star rating with no words before billing, so you pay only for reviews that say something. Use for "reviews with text", sentiment analysis, complaint triage.

includeAppRow.title: Include an app row
includeAppRow.description: true (default) = one free app row per app, language and country: app_name, developer, category, content_rating, rating_avg, rating_count, price, currency, icon, description. Never charged. Use for "Google Play rating of app X" or a daily rating history; false = review rows only.
includeAppRow.sectionDescription: What else goes into the dataset besides the review rows.

sessions.title: Parallel sessions
sessions.description: Parallel proxy sessions (egress IPs), 1-16; default 4. Google allows about one request a second per IP and answers up to 100 reviews per request, so 4 sessions read a few hundred reviews a second. Raise it for large runs; it changes speed, not cost.
sessions.sectionDescription: Leave these alone unless a run is being throttled; they change speed, not cost.

perIp.title: Requests per second per IP
perIp.description: Requests per second per session, 0.1-3; default 1. Google refuses bursts above about 1 per second per IP and the fetcher then rotates and backs off, so a higher value earns retries, not speed.

proxyConfiguration.title: Proxy
proxyConfiguration.description: Default: Apify Proxy, datacentre group. Google Play's review call needs no login, but each IP is throttled at about one request a second, so a run of more than a few thousand reviews needs several IPs. Small runs work without a proxy.

description: Google Play reviews. Minimal input: {"appIds": ["com.whatsapp"]} or {"appUrls": ["https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.whatsapp"]} — at least one. App names are not accepted (Play has no open search): take the id= part of the Play URL. languages defaults to ["en"] and countries to ["us"]: every language × country pair is read separately. maxReviewsPerApp defaults to 100 per app, language and country (up to $0.40 per pair at $0.004 a review); 0 = every review Google pages out.
